functions.name: core_otp_size
functions.brief: Total OTP size in bytes for this Core (0 where unavailable).

functions.name: core_otp_slot_addr
functions.brief: Absolute address of a slot (no bounds check).

functions.name: core_otp_read
functions.signature: core_otp_read(uint32_t offset, void * buf, uint32_t len)
functions.brief: Read bytes from OTP into `buf`. Memory-mapped load; no unlock needed. Returns 0 on success, -1 if the range is out of bounds or OTP is unavailable on this Core.

functions.name: core_otp_slot_is_blank
functions.brief: Return 1 if `slot` is entirely erased (all 0xFF), 0 if any bit is programmed, or -1 if the slot index is out of range / OTP unavailable. A blank slot is programmable; a non-blank slot is not (write-once).

functions.name: core_otp_program_slot
functions.brief: Program one 16-byte quad-word slot (write-once) and verify the read-back. IRREVERSIBLE. Refuses a slot that is not blank (returns -2) so a second write can't corrupt an existing record. On WBA55 this unlocks flash, issues a single 128-bit quad-word program, re-locks, and confirms the stored bytes match `rec`. There is no retry and no undo — callers should treat a failure as "advance to the next slot", not "try again here". slot: 0 .. CORE_OTP_SLOT_COUNT-1 rec:  pointer to exactly CORE_OTP_SLOT_SIZE (16) bytes. Returns 0 on success, -1 on range/program/verify error, -2 if the slot is not blank, -3 if OTP programming is unavailable on this Core. Deliberately NOT `@studio expose`d: a destructive, irreversible burn does not belong in the DSL palette. It is escape-to-C only (see @studio unsupported below).
